findings.rootCause: LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.supply only took the independent HashJoinIteration path for a sub-select optional part when the OPTIONAL had no condition (`!leftJoin.hasCondition() && TupleExprs.containsSubquery(rightArg)`); with a FILTER it fell back to the correlated LeftJoinIterator, which evaluates the optional part once per left row with the left row as input, and ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep forwarded that row into the sub-select body. A variable the sub-select does not project (fresh under bottom-up semantics) was therefore pre-bound, ORDER BY/LIMIT selected among pre-filtered rows and COUNT counted only compatible rows. The same leak existed without a condition for `OPTIONAL { { SELECT ... } ?t :z ?y }` because containsSubquery stops at a Join and the Join step only protects its right arg; badly designed inputs went through BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator, which is itself correlated.
findings.change: LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep routes every optional part that is a bottom-up scope boundary (BindingScopeAnalysis.isOutOfScopeForOptionalCorrelation: sub-select or MINUS in the current scope; deliberately NOT the parser's `{A} UNION {B}` scope-change flag, per critique 3.4.1 major, so the bounded adaptive/memoized UNION paths stay) to a HashJoinIteration(BuildSide.RIGHT) that evaluates the optional part exactly once with the OPTIONAL's own input and applies the condition as a residual predicate on every candidate: HashJoinIteration got a `Predicate<BindingSet> residualCondition` constructor (a probe row survives alone iff no compatible build row satisfies it; candidates still flow through the compatibility iterator so the candidate counters keep seeing rejected rows). The residual uses ScopedQueryValueEvaluationStep over leftJoin.getBindingNames() UNION lateralSubstitutedNames (critique 3.4.1 minor) with error-as-false and LEFT_JOIN_CONDITION_REJECTED_ROWS_ACTUAL telemetry like the post-filter, and the branch publishes its algorithm name. Badly designed inputs are handled bottom-up around the independent step by the new BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator.scopeFiltered (filtered input, compatibility check, problem-variable re-extension; the correlated iterator's post-processing was extracted into extendWithProblemVars). The Join-variant (sub-select as left arg of a Join inside the OPTIONAL) is closed by 3.4.3's sub-select scope boundary: the correlated LeftJoinIterator/JoinIterator may push the left row, but the nested sub-select unit withholds it. Two existing LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStepTest methods that asserted the correlated LeftJoinIterator for a conditioned sub-select OPTIONAL were renamed and now expect HashJoinIteration with the same (left-row-alone) result, as the design's existingTestsAtRisk prescribes.

findings.rootCause: Two cooperating leaks. (1) FilterIterator.evaluateSubstitutedExists cloned the EXISTS body and ran BindingAssignerOptimizer.optimize, whose VarVisitor replaces every bound Var with no scope awareness, so `?t :r ?x` inside a nested `SELECT ?t` became `?t :r 1` although x is not projected and is a fresh variable inside the sub-select. (2) Independently of substitution, the compiled body was evaluated with the outer row and ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep forwarded it into the sub-select body (GroupIterator evaluates the aggregate argument with parentBindings), which is also the mechanism behind 3.4.1's Join-variant and behind correlated MINUS over sub-selects. The nested ProjectionIterator additionally overwrote conflicting parent bindings instead of rejecting the row (critique missed finding).
findings.change: Following the critique instead of the design where they differ: (a) BindingAssignerOptimizer.substituteInScope(TupleExpr, BindingSet) is a new scoped substitution (ScopedVarVisitor) that replaces a Var wherever it is in scope but, inside a Projection/MultiProjection, only Vars whose name is a projected source name of that projection and of every enclosing projection (nested sub-selects intersect the visible set); non-projected variables are fresh by construction and stay untouched, projected ones are substituted before the sub-select's LIMIT/aggregation as the SPARQL 1.2 / EXISTS-CG substitute() requires (critique 3.4.3 major; pinned by existsOverLimitedSubSelectSubstitutesProjectedVariableBeforeTheLimit and existsOverGroupedSubSelectSubstitutesProjectedGroupKey). optimize() for external bindings is unchanged. (b) The runtime scope boundary is placed at the ROOT of the nested sub-select unit (the Projection plus the Slice/Distinct/Reduced/Order the parser stacks above it), not at the Projection: BindingScopeAnalysis.isNestedSubSelectRoot(node) identifies such a root (isSubquery() Projection unit with an ancestor other than QueryRoot/DescribeOperator/MaterializeTupleExpr; parentless or top-level units keep pass-through of external bindings) and DefaultEvaluationStrategy.precompile wraps the compiled unit in the new SubSelectScopeBoundaryQueryEvaluationStep: the unit is evaluated with only BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames (constants by LATERAL definition), NO other incoming binding is pushed (no pre-binding of projected names at all, so the critique's Slice-above-Projection blocker cannot occur), and the rows are joined with the incoming bindings afterwards by compatibility on every name (conflicting rows dropped, never overwritten; compatible rows extended). Because the check happens above the Slice, LIMIT/DISTINCT/aggregation stay bottom-up (projectedNamesAreJoinedByCompatibilityAfterTheSubSelectIsComplete, subSelectAsLeftArgOfAJoinInsideAnOptionalIsEvaluatedBottomUp, and the memory Join-variant cases). (c) evaluateSubstitutedExists clones under an `Exists` holder before precompiling (design (c)); the critique argued the holder becomes unnecessary, but the code proves it still is: without a parent the clone's sub-select is a top-level unit and would pass the outer row through, re-introducing leak (2); the holder also makes the clone compile exactly like the original body (isPartOfSubQuery scoping of inner filters). ProjectionIterator itself is unchanged: its nested/outer notion now only decides whether the (already restricted) parent bindings are copied in, so the two notions cannot disagree on results. No kill switch was added although the design recommended one (see followUps).

findings.rootCause: FilterIterator trusted the planner's `optimizer.semiAntiKind = minus-assured-shared` stamp: inside supplyMaterializedExistsSemiJoin the flag only relaxed the root scope-change check, after which the MINUS body was treated exactly like an EXISTS body (per-probe evaluateSubstitutedExists substituting ALL left-row bindings, including names that are out of scope inside a MINUS operand such as `?o` in `MINUS { ?s :q ?v FILTER(?v = ?o) }`; materialization parameters = every referenced variable). Result: the hinted anti-join removed rows MINUS keeps. Worse (critique 3.4.4 major), that branch was not even the only path: a scope-changed filter, a filter nested in an EXISTS body, the fused VALUES-join filter, a `streaming-exists` hint or a kind-only stamp without an algorithm hint all reached the generic FilterIterator/ExistsQueryValueEvaluationStep and were evaluated with NOT EXISTS substitution semantics.
findings.change: FilterIterator.supply now starts with supplyAssuredSharedMinusAntiJoin, before the fused VALUES join and before every decline rule, so a rewritten MINUS can never reach the generic filter. For a `Not(Exists(body))` filter with the kind it re-checks the rewrite certificate (roadmap 4.2/4.6) with assuredSharedMinusNames: shared = MinusQueryEvaluationStep.sharedOutputBindingNames(left, body) minus constant var names, must be non-empty and assured on BOTH sides, and fv(body) ∩ pv(left) ⊆ shared (the 3.2.1 precondition; a left-bound variable the operand references without sharing is fresh inside a MINUS operand but a correlation inside a probe). If the certificate fails the filter is evaluated by a real `new MinusQueryEvaluationStep(arg, existsArg, left, body)` (the node carries the semantic kind, so MINUS is always the right fallback) and the disposition `declined:minus-hint-invalid` is recorded. If it holds, the anti-join is built with sharedBindingNames = correlationKeyBindingNames = shared, materializationParameterBindingNames = empty (materialize once, unbound; MaterializedExistsFilterIteration.matches is then exactly MINUS compatibility on assured shared names) and a probe that evaluates the body with `BindingScopeAnalysis.retain(row, shared)` and never substitutes; the planned mode is honoured only for compatibility-selection-safe bodies, any other body is forced to MATERIALIZED. The common construction tail of the semi-join was extracted into materializedExistsStep so both paths share it; the old hint-trusting relaxation of containsVariableScopeChange was removed. MinusQueryEvaluationStep.sharedOutputBindingNames is exposed as @InternalUseOnly public static. Other Filter shapes stamped with the kind (not Not(Exists)) are left on the normal path. semanticKind() telemetry (MINUS_ASSURED_SHARED) is unchanged (FilterIteratorTelemetryTest#safeMinusRecordsItsOwnSemanticKind stays green).

wp1/wp2/wp9 (rewrites that reason about sub-select scope): the executor now treats every nested sub-select unit (Slice/Distinct/Reduced/Order over an isSubquery Projection, inside any operator) as a bottom-up boundary that withholds correlated input except LATERAL-substituted names and joins projected names by compatibility afterwards (BindingScopeAnalysis.isNestedSubSelectRoot + SubSelectScopeBoundaryQueryEvaluationStep).
